papers.title: Analysis of an all-to-all connected star array of transmon qubits
papers.abstract: We analyzed quantum $XX$ and $ZZ$ coupling and state transfer in an all-to-all connected star array of capacitively coupled superconducting transmon qubits. It is shown that in a highly-connected system like this a variety of different $ZZ$ couplings arise that correspond to the different ways qubits can interact with each other, opening different channels for unwanted qubit crosstalk and thus qubit operation errors. We studied the dependence of both the $XX$ and the $ZZ$ coupling on qubit detuning that controls qubit-qubit interaction. The $XX$ coupling, quantified by the error state occupation probability, shows a $Δω^{-2}$ decay with qubit detuning $Δω$. On the other hand, all $ZZ$ coupling frequencies show spikes at values in the lower detuning region that correspond to resonances between qubit states and states out of the computational basis, after which all couplings quickly decay to zero as qubit detuning further increases. This allows to define an operational region where near-zero qubit coupling can be achieved. We derive equations for the couplings as a function of qubit detuning that agree with numerical results solving the Schrödinger equation.

summary.summary: This paper analyzes quantum $XX$ and $ZZ$ couplings in a capacitively coupled three-transmon-qubit star array using dressed-state perturbation theory and numerical solutions of the Schrödinger equation. The work demonstrates that highly-connected systems exhibit multiple types of $ZZ$ couplings (three pairwise and one all-to-all) that create crosstalk channels and identifies detuning regimes where couplings can be suppressed.
summary.motivation: Understanding qubit-qubit interactions in fully-connected architectures is essential for implementing high-connectivity quantum processors and quantum simulations with superconducting qubits, where unwanted $ZZ$ coupling leads to operation errors that scale with system connectivity.
summary.method:
Dressed-state perturbation theory to first order in the coupling amplitudes $K_{ij}$, with analytical expressions derived for both degenerate and detuned qubits, validated against full Schrödinger equation solutions for transmons with $I_c = 40$ nA, $C = 100$ fF, $C_x = 1$ fF, and $
u_{qb}/(2 eta) = 6$ GHz.
summary.result: For degenerate qubits, the $XX$ coupling is $\_XX/(2 eta) \approx 30$ MHz while pairwise $ZZ$ couplings reach $\approx 1.89$ MHz and the all-to-all $ZZ$ coupling reaches $\approx 4.7$ MHz; the error state occupation probability decays as $\Delta\omega^{-2}$ with detuning, while all $ZZ$ couplings show resonant spikes at detuning values determined by qubit anharmonicity before decaying to near-zero above $\approx 200$ MHz.

papers.title: Energy relaxation via quantum thermalization: A superconducting qubit coupled to an interacting many-body two-level system
papers.abstract: Two-level systems (TLS) are widely recognized as a dominant source of energy relaxation in superconducting qubits, limiting coherence times and device performance. While TLS-induced dissipation is often modeled as independent channels, interacting TLS can form finite many-body environments whose dynamical role in qubit relaxation remains insufficiently understood. Building on the information-erasure-based framework for irreversible thermalization developed in our previous work, we present a microscopic model and numerical simulations of a superconducting qubit coupled to a finite interacting many-body TLS environment as a concrete physical realization of this mechanism. We show that effective irreversible energy relaxation can emerge from intrinsic many-body dynamics without invoking external baths or phenomenological dissipation. The introduction of information erasure drives a transition from coherent oscillatory energy exchange to nonoscillatory exponential relaxation of the qubit. The relaxation times exhibit the scaling $T_1, T_2 \propto J_{q,τ}^{-2}$ with respect to the qubit-TLS coupling strength, consistent with Fermi's golden rule and Lindblad-type descriptions. Importantly, both exponential decay and its scaling behavior arise directly from microscopic many-body dynamics. These results provide quantitative insight into TLS-induced decoherence mechanisms and establish a microscopic link between information erasure, many-body thermalization, and irreversible relaxation in superconducting quantum systems.

summary.summary: This work demonstrates that irreversible exponential energy relaxation in a superconducting qubit emerges from intrinsic many-body thermalization of an interacting TLS environment, without external baths or phenomenological dissipation. The relaxation times exhibit $T_1, T_2 \propto J_{q,\tau}^{-2}$ scaling consistent with Fermi's golden rule, arising directly from unitary many-body dynamics driven by stochastic frequency fluctuations (FFTIE sequence) that enable information erasure.
summary.motivation: TLS are dominant decoherence sources in superconducting qubits, yet the microscopic origin of irreversible relaxation from coherent qubit-TLS interactions in finite interacting environments remains unclear, especially when TLS dissipation into phonons is suppressed.
summary.method: A superconducting qubit is coupled ($J_{q,\tau}/2\pi = 0.002$–$0.1$ MHz) to a 7-site 1D chain of interacting TLS ($J_\tau = J_\upsilon/2\pi = 1$ MHz, $U_{\tau,\upsilon}/2\pi = -0.2$ MHz) with stochastic frequency fluctuations applied via alternating unitary evolution and random-Hamiltonian segments (forward-time information-erasure sequence).
summary.result: Extracted $T_1$ values range from $975.88$ µs (at $J_{q,\tau}/2\pi = 0.01$ MHz) to $24536.80$ µs (at $J_{q,\tau}/2\pi = 0.002$ MHz), with $T_1 \propto J_{q,\tau}^{-1.997}$ and $T_2 \approx 2.14 T_1$; relaxation transitions from exponential decay to oscillatory decay as coupling increases to $J_{q,\tau}/2\pi = 0.1$ MHz ($T_1 = 13.0$ µs), demonstrating suppression of coherent backflow via many-body thermalization.
